chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Ghalib, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Hajj and the Umrah are two markets from the markets of the Hereafter, and the one who performs them is in the Neighbourhood of Allah. If he realises what he hopes for, Allah will forgive him, and if his term is cut short, his reward falls upon Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Hajj and Umrah as markets of the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, the metaphor of Hajj and Umrah as 'markets of the Hereafter' (aswaq al-akhirah) highlights the transactional nature of spiritual investment, where the pilgrim trades worldly efforts for eternal gain. This narration, found in al-Kafi, underscores the divine guarantee of reward, affirming that even if death interrupts the ritual, the merit is fully secured by Allah, reflecting the concept of 'amal al-mu'allaq' (suspended action) being fully compensated.
